seed.name: congenital multicore myopathy with external ophthalmoplegia

partners.mechanism_chain: RYR1 (HGNC:10483) —DISRUPTS→ Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0001733); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0001733) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0001733) —LEADS_TO→ External ophthalmoplegia (HP:0000590); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0001733) —LEADS_TO→ Central core (HP:0003701). Mutations in RYR1 disrupt the normal function of the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release channel. This aberrant calcium handling leads to the common phenotype of muscle weakness, and also contributes to the more specific phenotypes of external ophthalmoplegia in one disease and the characteristic central core structure in the other.

partners.mechanism_chain: RYR1 (loss-of-function variant) (HGNC:10483) —DISRUPTS→ Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release Dysregulation; RYR1 (gain-of-function variant) (HGNC:10483) —DISRUPTS→ Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release Dysregulation; Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release Dysregulation —LEADS_TO→ Congenital myopathy (HP:0003198); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release Dysregulation —LEADS_TO→ External ophthalmoplegia (HP:0000603); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release Dysregulation —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release Dysregulation —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004322); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release Dysregulation —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0002670). Mutations in RYR1 lead to dysregulation of calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum. In congenital multicore myopathy, this is often due to haploinsufficiency, resulting in muscle weakness and ophthalmoplegia. In King-Denborough syndrome, gain-of-function mutations cause similar, but more variable, phenotypes including muscle weakness, short stature, and skeletal abnormalities, all stemming from aberrant calcium handling.

#### 1. central core myopathy  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.754)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2672351, Reactome:R-HSA-5578775)

**Proposed mechanism:** RYR1 (HGNC:10483) —DISRUPTS→ Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0001733); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0001733) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0001733) —LEADS_TO→ External ophthalmoplegia (HP:0000590); Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Calcium Release (GO:0001733) —LEADS_TO→ Central core (HP:0003701). Mutations in RYR1 disrupt the normal function of the sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release channel. This aberrant calcium handling leads to the common phenotype of muscle weakness, and also contributes to the more specific phenotypes of external ophthalmoplegia in one disease and the characteristic central core structure in the other.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in RYR1 that consistently lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects in both disease contexts, or the absence of RYR1 variants in a significant proportion of patients with either condition. _(variant: A pathogenic variant in RYR1 with a gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01% would challenge its role as a rare causal variant for these myopathies.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism in RYR1-related myopathies can facilitate the development of targeted therapies for both congenital multicore myopathy with external ophthalmoplegia and central core myopathy, potentially by modulating calcium handling or downstream pathways affected by RYR1 dysfunction.

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2672351, Reactome:R-HSA-5578775)

Mutations in RYR1 lead to dysregulation of calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum. In congenital multicore myopathy, this is often due to haploinsufficiency, resulting in muscle weakness and ophthalmoplegia. In King-Denborough syndrome, gain-of-function mutations cause similar, but more variable, phenotypes including muscle weakness, short stature, and skeletal abnormalities, all stemming from aberrant calcium handling.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in RYR1 with loss-of-function mechanisms in King-Denborough syndrome patients, or gain-of-function mechanisms in congenital multicore myopathy patients, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: N/A)_
